text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Crown Prince Hassan arrives in Washington for talks with President Clinton and top U.S. officials. Aid to Jordan expected to increase by $100 million in 1997.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali says France and Holland to grant Jordan $69 million.
- Military court continues trial of Ahmed Daqamsa, hears testimony from four Israelis.
- Jordan passes on to Syria Turkish assurances that its withdrawal from northern Iraq has started.

- 55 percent of people seeking work in ministries and government organisations already work for the private sector, report for social security fund finds. Report says their names should be removed from government figures to give a truer reflection of the unemployment rate.
- Jordanian ambassador to Israel says heavy-handed Israeli security is obstructing diplomats.
- Hamas political chief Musa Abu Marzook says no changes expected in Hamas leadership either inside or outside the West Bank and Gaza Strip -- and if there were he wouldn't tell the media anyway.

- Clinton to promise Crown Prince Hassan $500 million over five years. For the first time in the history of the region, Jordan will become an equal partner to Egypt and Israel in America's Middle East commitments and priorities.
- Majali says France pledges $60 million to Jordan, Netherlands pledge $9 million as a result of King Hussein's European tour.
- Government to reform seven state loan funds, merging funds which perform similar operations, Deputy Prime Minister Abdullah Ensour says.
- Jordan not expelling Egyptian workers, acting Labour Minister Mohammad Kheir Mamsar says. 75,000 have already got their papers in order ahead of government deadline for the end of this week.
- Crown Prince to convey Jordan's stand to Washington over U.S. Congress decision to consider Jerusalem the united capital of Israel.
- Iranian official says problem with Jordan is its ties with Israel.
